title: Claude Was Trained on Protein Sequences at Scale (LLM-bioseq-probe)
authors: Xinming Tu and Leo Tianlai Chen
models_tested: GPT-6.2 Sol / Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.5
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen 3.8, Kimi K3.1 Pro, GLM-5.3, MiniMax M3, gpt-oss-120b, Nemotron 3 Ultra
code_and_data_released: MIT-licensed repository with test sets, evaluation scripts, gzipped raw JSONL model replies, and figure code.

methods.datasets: Main set: 668 unreviewed TrEMBL bacterial/archaeal proteins from 167 Pfam Domains of Unknown Function (no PDB structure, <=3 Europe PMC hits, UniRef90 singletons, 5 cuts/protein = 3,340 cuts). Family-size set: +90 smaller families (257 total). Post-cutoff set (Appendix G): 56 RefSeq proteins first public 2-27 Aug 2026 with <50% UniRef50 identity to earlier clusters (34-49% closest relative). Contact maps (Appendix H): 46 post-Aug-2026 PDBs (only 2 strictly clean) + 6 controls.
methods.evaluation_protocol: Prefix-only next-amino-acid completion (model outputs 10 AAs; 1st AA scored) paired with accession-seeded shuffled copies at identical cut sites. Temperature 0 where accepted, lowest thinking, no tools, 1 sample/cut.
methods.controls_included: Shuffled composition-matched controls, 128 zero-paper Pfam families, family-size scaling across 257 families, strict post-cutoff <50% identity RefSeq holdout (Appendix G), and copy-then-continue check.
methods.compute_and_tools: Zero external tools; thinking tokens appeared in only 9% of Fable 5.2 replies (non-thinking scored higher: 54.7% vs 48.2%). Total API cost ~$730.
methods.metrics: Family-mean real-minus-shuffled next-AA accuracy gap (percentage points) with 10,000-resample 95% bootstrap CI and Spearman r vs log(family size); top-N long-range contact precision (|i-j| >= 24, Cb <= 8 A).

key_results.metric: Real minus shuffled next-AA accuracy (pp, 95% CI)
key_results.llm_score: Fable 5.2 +45.1 (42.5 to 47.6; 54.1% vs 9.0%); Opus 5.5 +27.4; GPT/Gemini/open LLMs -0.0 to +2.9
key_results.notes: Holds in 128 zero-paper families (+45.9 Fable 5.2) and scales with family size (Spearman 0.38-0.50), providing strong controlled evidence of large-scale protein sequence pretraining in Claude 5.2/5.5.

key_results.benchmark: 56 post-cutoff Aug 2026 RefSeq proteins (<50% UniRef50 ID)
key_results.llm_model: Claude Fable 5.2 / Claude Opus 5.5 / GPT-6.2 Sol
key_results.notes: Rules out exact sequence memorization as the sole explanation; generalizes across <50% identity family relatives.
44/46 post-Aug-2026 PDBs had pre-cutoff sequences or earlier PDB homologs, leaving only 2 strictly clean targets; Fable trails ESM-2 650M substantially.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: Appendix G specifically tests 56 RefSeq proteins first public 2-27 Aug 2026 after assumed July 2026 cutoff (+22.1 pp for Fable 5.2); Appendix H contact maps note only 2/46 targets are strictly clean.

homology_overlap.evidence: Main set uses UniRef90 singletons; Appendix G enforces <50% identity to earlier UniRef50 clusters (closest earlier relative 34-49%).

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: Unreviewed TrEMBL DUF families with no PDB structures and <=3 Europe PMC hits; 128 zero-paper families score +45.9 pp (Spearman 0.05 vs paper count).

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Composition-matched shuffled controls, repeat consistency check (57.5% vs 57.5%), 0.1% non-answer rate, and copy-then-continue control; Fable 5 excluded due to 44% policy blocks.

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Pure intrinsic next-residue and contact-list outputs.

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Zero tools, temp 0, minimal thinking; non-thinking Fable 5.2 replies outperformed thinking replies (54.7% vs 48.2%).

baseline_fairness.evidence: Autoregressive pLMs (ProGen3-3B, ProtGPT3-10B) receive identical prefix-only context; masked ESM-2 650M evaluated both prefix-only (+7.0) and bidirectional (+34.6).

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: All data, scripts, raw JSONL outputs, and figure code released under MIT license.

critiques_and_commentary.author: Hacker News discussion
critiques_and_commentary.summary: Debated whether shuffled sequences are a sufficient baseline control vs Markov/di-residue controls; authors noted composition and copy-then-continue checks plus family-size scaling.

takeaway: Claude Fable 5.2 (+45.1 pp main, +22.1 pp on post-cutoff <50%-identity RefSeq proteins) and Opus 5.5 (+27.4 / +13.4 pp) match or exceed open autoregressive pLMs (ProGen3-3B +32.5 / +12.0) on unstudied DUF proteins while GPT-6, Gemini 4, and open-weight LLMs stay near zero. On long-range contact maps, however, Fable 5.2 (~25%) trails ESM-2 650M (~67%) and only 2 of 46 targets are strictly free of pre-cutoff sequence/PDB relatives.
